items.text: Round 2 selections (D2.1=A, D2.2=A, D2.3=A, D2.4=A) baked into plan.md. Subpackage path is now concretely `api/domain/<name>/`; the execution subset is fixed at `ai`, `remote-profile`, `user-auth`, `metrics`; the deferred set is fixed at `landing`, `billing`, `downloads`, `admin`; cycle policy is revert-and-defer (explicitly forbids extracting `api/shared/` mid-execution); and the follow-up is a single `execute` backlog item.

Plan structural changes: collapsed prior 'Settled Decisions (Round 1)' section into 'Settled Decisions' with Round 1 + Round 2 subsections; removed the 'Pending Decisions (Round 2)' block entirely; concretized Target Files to list each `api/domain/<name>/` path; concretized Target End State / DoD / validation checklist to name the 4 subpackaged + 4 deferred domains; tightened Phase 2 cycle handling to match D2.3 (revert + defer, no new shared packages); added an explicit Out-of-Scope item and a Non-goals bullet forbidding new shared packages; tightened the ARCHITECTURE.md transitional callout requirement to name the 4 deferred domains.

Readiness scored 3/3 across all five dimensions. Problem statement is concrete with file:line evidence; scope is bounded and includes a clean in/out list plus a forbidden-pattern list; approach has a defined sequence with cycle-handling rule; testing covers vrooli scenario test + per-domain smoke + docs-health threshold; risks enumerate the realistic failure modes (cycles, route-drop, mixed state, doc drift, artifact deletion, restart failure) with concrete mitigations. The plan is ready to queue for execution.

No initiative context to reconcile: this backlog item is not part of an initiative, so there are no sibling members or upstream/downstream items whose sequencing this plan needs to flag for the orchestrator. The follow-up `execute` item planned in Phase 6 will be a standalone successor.

plan_updates: Baked Round 2 decisions (D2.1-D2.4 all option A) into plan.md: concretized subpackage path to `api/domain/<name>/`, named the 4 subpackaged + 4 deferred domains throughout, hardened the cycle policy to revert-and-defer with an explicit prohibition on new shared packages, narrowed the follow-up to a single `execute` item, and removed the now-resolved Pending Decisions section.
